title: The Krishna in the ballast clay
hookLine: a ship in a storm, a monk on the shore, and a lump of clay with Krishna inside
carry: dvaita: God, souls and world are truly two
last: FIVE SHEATHS, AND THE ONE WHO SEES THEM.

lines: A SHIP IN A STORM OFF UDUPI.
cards: A trading ship is caught in a storm off the coast of Karnataka, near Udupi. A monk standing on the beach, the story goes, waves his cloth, and the ship comes safely in. The grateful captain offers him anything on board.
The monk asks for one thing: a big lump of pale clay the sailors had been using as ballast. They break it open, and inside is an image of Krishna, holding a churning rope.
That image, tradition says, is the one still worshiped in the Krishna temple at Udupi today. The monk was Madhva.

teach.b: Tradition places Madhva in the thirteenth century. He founded a school of Vedanta called Tattvavada, the teaching of what's real. Today it's usually called Dvaita: two.
Where Shankara said not two, Madhva said two, clearly and forever. God is one reality. You are another.
The world is another, and it's real, not a snake on a rope.
Madhva spelled out five differences that never go away: God from souls, God from matter, each soul from every other soul, souls from matter, and each bit of matter from every other.
God, for Madhva, is Vishnu, and only God is independent. Everything else, you, me, the clay, depends on God, moment by moment. Not as a snake depends on a rope, a mistake.

As a child depends on a parent: really there, really held. And here's what that gives devotion. Madhva's followers put it this way: if you and God were finally one, love would be only a stage on the way.
Advaitins answer that differently, as you heard. For Madhva, the difference is the truth, so the love can last.
Even a freed soul doesn't dissolve into God. It stays itself, in God's presence, loving and serving. The lover and the beloved stay two, and the space between them isn't a wall.

teach.h: DVAITA: GOD, SOULS AND WORLD ARE TRULY TWO.
teach.b: That's Dvaita, and it's why so many Hindu devotees call themselves God's servant, dasa, and never expect to become God. Advaita and Dvaita are both alive today, and neither is ranked here.

how: Followers of Madhva, the Madhva Vaishnavas, centered on Udupi in Karnataka, worship Krishna as Vishnu, study Madhva's commentaries, and understand the soul as eternally distinct from and dependent on God.

p: found Krishna in a lump of clay

s: Madhva taught that the world is like a snake seen on a rope
for Madhva the world is real, and distinct from God.
in Dvaita, a liberated soul merges into God
it stays itself, forever distinct, in God's presence.
Madhva's five differences include soul from soul
God and souls, God and matter, soul and soul, soul and matter, matter and matter.

games.q: you're Madhva on the beach. the captain of the ship you helped offers you anything on board. what does tradition say you ask for?
games.why: the ballast clay. inside was an image of Krishna, which tradition says is the one worshiped at Udupi.

practice: Think of someone you love who is really, stubbornly not you: they laugh at different things, want different things. Notice that the love lives exactly in that difference; if they were you, there'd be no one to love.
Feel the space between you as room, not distance. If you pray, turn that same warmth toward God, as other than you, and near.

wordCard.voice: Dvaita, two. God, souls and the world are really distinct, only God is independent, and the freed soul stays itself, loving God forever.

orig.note: Sanskrit: dvaita, duality, twoness; the name for Madhva's school, which he called tattvavada.

carryVoice: Your line: dvaita, God, souls and world are truly two. A real God, a real you, and room between for love. Day two eighty-eight, done.
